correctness.rationale: Gauss angle Jacobian rho=h+h″ establishes f=rho/L; all cyclic gaps less than pi iff the halfplane intersection is bounded. When a single gap equals pi-delta, the divergent vertex has leading w(theta)/delta and shoelace area w(theta)^2/(2 delta). Every side is tangent so perimeter bounds area by a sum of reciprocal near-pi gap defects, and two-gap simplex estimates make concurrent extremes negligible in the leading t^-1 probability. Adjacent-pair density n(n-1) f(theta)f(theta+pi) H(theta)^(n-2) gives the exact integral constant after division by p_n>0. Positive constant yields the q<1 iff moment threshold. The noncircle constant-width example follows by trigonometric integrals; finite numerical evaluations check its sign but do not prove the general claim.
residual_risks: Requires fixed n>=3, positive continuous normal density, strictly convex smooth support with positive curvature; no generality for flats/offsets.
Uniform estimates at simultaneous gaps demand care; the supplied bounded-density/simplex-volume decomposition explicitly addresses the leading-order contribution.

value.rationale: A natural stochastic-geometric question is whether a random tangent polygon enclosing a smooth convex curve has finite conditional mean, and what geometry controls its tail. The nontrivial exactly shape-dependent all-n coefficient and the constant-width counterexample isolate information beyond width while explaining an otherwise counterintuitive infinite mean. Neither circle tail nor arbitrary positive-density extension alone would give that shape comparison.
residual_risks: It does not provide second-order errors or statistical estimators; geometries beyond smooth positive-curvature bodies remain outside scope.

limitations: The circle 1/t formula is not a new contribution; the general coefficient, moment dichotomy and constant-width separation are reviewed.
